definitions.explanation: A small olive-brown bird native to Japan, famous for its distinctive call ホーホケキョ. Associated with spring and considered one of Japan's most beloved birds.

examples.japanese: {鶯|うぐいす}が{鳴|な}いている。
{春|はる}になると{鶯|うぐいす}の{声|こえ}が{聞|き}こえてくる。
examples.english: When spring comes, you can hear the voice of the bush warbler.

examples.japanese: {早朝|そうちょう}、{庭|にわ}の{梅|うめ}の{木|き}に{止|と}まった{鶯|うぐいす}がホーホケキョと{鳴|な}き、{春|はる}の{訪|おとず}れを{告|つ}げた。
examples.english: Early in the morning, a bush warbler perched on the plum tree in the garden and called "hōhokekyo," announcing the arrival of spring.

notes:
The uguisu is considered a herald of spring in Japanese culture. Its call ホーホケキョ is one of the most recognized bird sounds in Japan.

CULTURAL NOTE:
- {鶯|うぐいす}は{春告鳥|はるつげどり} (spring-heralding bird) as a poetic name
- {梅|うめ}に{鶯|うぐいす} ({梅|うめ}と{鶯|うぐいす}): plum blossom and bush warbler — a classic pairing in Japanese art and poetry symbolizing early spring
- {鶯|うぐいす}の{初音|はつね}: the first call of the bush warbler in the new year — a classic seasonal theme

COMMON EXPRESSIONS:
- {鶯|うぐいす}が{鳴|な}く: the bush warbler sings
- {鶯|うぐいす}{色|いろ}: bush warbler color (yellow-green)
